top_story_title: Cisco orders emergency distrust of eMudhra CAs after intermediate private keys proved brute-forceable in seconds
top_story_summary: Between 17 and 20 October 2026 a researcher demonstrated that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates are fundamentally broken, the result of an error in eMudhra's April 2025 Key Generation Ceremony. Cisco's advisory states the keys can be brute-forced within seconds. That is not a theoretical weakness in a CA's process - it means anyone willing to spend the compute can hold the signing key of a publicly trusted intermediate and mint a certificate for any name they like.
top_actions: Open the Cisco advisory and work its affected-product list against your asset inventory; Cisco states products absent from that list are not affected, so scope from the list rather than guessing.

Remove or distrust the eMudhra root and the eight intermediate CAs in device trust stores - firewalls, VPN gateways, load balancers, wireless controllers and management platforms - including any manually imported CA bundles.
Inventory your own certificates for anything chaining to eMudhra; reissue from a different CA and generate fresh key material rather than re-signing the existing key.
Audit certificate-based authentication paths specifically: EAP-TLS/802.1X, IPsec certificate auth, client certificates on admin portals. A forged intermediate-signed certificate defeats all of them.
Re-check the advisory over the coming days - Cisco states it will be updated as additional information becomes available.
executive_summary: Cisco issued an emergency informational advisory to distrust eMudhra root and intermediate CAs: private keys for eight intermediates can be brute-forced in seconds after a broken April 2025 key generation ceremony.

Palo Alto Networks is tracking the impact of two critical PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, on its products; the advisory is rated HIGH and the collected source names no fixed release.

A weekly roundup points to an exploited Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect VPN flaw, but gives no CVE or fixed build - treat internet-facing GlobalProtect portals as a priority and get the detail from the vendor advisory.
No AI-related network-device item in this window, and no new vendor AI-defence announcements.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Scope from the advisory's affected-product list against your asset inventory, filtered by model and running version; products not listed are stated as unaffected.

**Cisco** — Remove or distrust the eMudhra root and the eight intermediate CAs from device trust stores and from any manually imported CA bundles on firewalls, VPN gateways, load balancers, wireless controllers and management platforms.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Read the per-product impact table on the advisory and map it to the platforms and PAN-OS versions you run; the severity alone does not tell you which of your devices are in scope.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Apply the vendor fixed release once the advisory names one for your platform, or the documented workaround if a maintenance window is not available yet; in an HA pair, upgrade the secondary first.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Go to the Palo Alto Networks security advisories page and identify the GlobalProtect advisory behind this reference, including its CVE, affected versions and fixed build - do not act on the roundup's wording alone.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Patch to the vendor's fixed build once identified; until then, confirm whether the vendor documents a workaround or a mitigating configuration for GlobalProtect portals.
